A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Unmasking Trees for Tabular Data. Their readable text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison, including matching content across substantial additions and reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic case studies, imputation and generation results on 27 datasets, and quantization/BaltoBot ablations in Appendix A.

after.justification: v4 retains these original results and adds the authors' M5 forecasting results, expanded case-study comparisons, and dataset-level scores and runtimes.

M1.justification: Section 2.4 replaces Gaussian filling of missing TabPFN inputs with NanTabPFN: query-dependent selection of observed columns and compatible training rows, random feature removal when necessary, and a constant-feature fallback. This substantially changes the TabPFN variant's procedure. The core UnmaskingTrees and BaltoBot algorithms remain; their new pseudocode mainly expands documentation.

E1.justification: v4 adds M5 Walmart sales forecasting, predicting heavy-tailed unit sales from product attributes and sales history. This extends standalone probabilistic prediction beyond v2's synthetic wave and Poisson studies to a substantial real-world application. Two Moons, Iris, and the existing 27-dataset coverage remain.

E2.justification: The new M5 comparison includes Deep Ensembles, IBUG, NGBoost Poisson, and Quantile Regression Forests alongside Treeffuser, using explicitly attributed baseline scores. Figure 2 also adds MICE-Forest to the Iris comparison, although it already appeared in Two Moons. Comparator membership in the matched benchmark and ablation tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: M5 introduces 120,000 training and 10,000 test samples, CRPS/MAE/RMSE evaluation, 100 predictive draws for CRPS and 50 for conditional means, and tuned/untuned comparisons. Tuning uses 10 folds with 80/20 splits and 25 Bayesian optimization iterations. Existing benchmark protocols remain; the newly specified 20-bin ablation setting is additional disclosure, not an established setting change.

E4.justification: v4 adds tuned-versus-untuned M5 comparisons, runtime profiling against dataset size and dimensionality in Appendix C/Figure 5, and TabPFN panels in the Iris case study. The central k-Means/KDI/BaltoBot ablation is unchanged: v2 Tables 4–5 correspond to v4 Tables 2 and 6.

E5.justification: Matched benchmark and ablation tables retain three experiments per dataset, ten imputations where applicable, and standard-error reporting. M5 reports point estimates without confidence intervals, significance tests, or seed information; its folds concern tuning. The appendix variance and MAD columns measure imputation diversity rather than uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: All five v2 result tables retain their numerical values after matching and equivalent formatting. v4 adds M5 scores, Iris panels, and dataset-level scores and runtimes in Tables 7–10. On M5, tuned BaltoBot and Treeffuser both report CRPS 0.644, with RMSE 2.07 and 2.09 respectively. The wave text changes BaltoBoTabPFN from slightly worse to visually matching Treeffuser, despite retaining Figure 3.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 adds a permutation-averaged likelihood definition and states a connection to masked modeling with uniformly sampled masking rates. Section 2.4 defines NanTabPFN's admissible rows and columns mathematically. No theorem or proof is added, and the computational-complexity reasoning remains unchanged apart from depth-to-height notation.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal imputation and missing-data generation claims retain their meaning. The introduction and conclusion extend the claimed benefits of standalone probabilistic prediction to heavy-tailed sales forecasting, with the v4 conclusion claiming state-of-the-art results there.

C2.justification: The new Limitations section discloses UnmaskingTabPFN's slowness and out-of-memory failures, restricting practical applicability to very small datasets. Section 3.2 emphasizes the benchmark's small-dataset scope, and Appendix C discusses dataset-dependent runtime differences. The earlier appeal to unmasking versus denoising in self-supervised learning is removed; most mechanism discussion remains.

D1.justification: v4 adds three algorithm listings, categorical softmax/cross-entropy details, default XGBoost settings, hardware specifications, 20-bin ablation details, M5 tuning ranges, and explicit baseline-score provenance. Appendix C supplies dataset dimensions and runtimes. The earlier 1024-sample TabPFN subsampling description is omitted; the code-access link is unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 substantially expands references and attribution for imputation/generation baselines, probabilistic forecasters, and foundational flow/diffusion methods. It foregrounds XLNet/permutation modeling in the method's lineage and contrasts its efficient tree implementations with Transformer-based TabMT and newly cited DP-TBART. The Balestriero–LeCun citation and associated argument are removed.

P1.justification: Beyond adding experiments, v4 expands the method exposition and reorganizes Section 3.2 into fuller imputation and generation accounts, rewrites Section 2.4 and the conclusion, and introduces a separate Limitations section. Ablation material moves into the main text, while the appendix is reorganized into algorithms, raw ablations, and dataset-level results.

P2.justification: Figure 2 changes from eight plots in two columns to eleven plots plus a legend in four columns, adding MICE-Forest and TabPFN panels. v4 adds the M5 table, Tables 7–10, Figure 5, and three algorithm displays, and relocates the ablation rank table into the main text. Figures 3–4 retain their underlying graphics.

improvement.justification: v4 addresses an important validation gap: v2 supported standalone probabilistic prediction mainly through synthetic demonstrations, whereas Section 3.4 adds a documented real-world M5 comparison against diverse predictors. Expanded algorithm descriptions, score provenance, hardware and dataset-level reporting, and explicit TabPFN limitations substantially improve assessability and reproducibility information. M5's missing uncertainty estimates and the different hardware used for runtime comparisons still limit claims about small performance margins and comparative speed.
